description: Attack the panel-factor bottleneck (now ~63-83% of the global-best 7468us kernel, latency-bound at 0.72 waves/SM) with a COOPERATIVE MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX panel: a communication-avoiding TSQR-style factorization where 2-4 CTAs (a thread-block cluster) split the tall panel by rows, each factors its row-block, then they combine the small R-blocks via a reduction tree, sharing partial reflectors through distributed shared memory / global scratch. This exposes the row-parallelism the current serial single-CTA panel starves on (the panel is tall: m up to 1024+ rows, cb=32-64 cols), raising occupancy past 1 wave/SM. Fork off the current best so the fast bmm trailing update and T-factor are inherited; keep n in {32,176,352,512,1024} on the custom path and everything else on geqrf.

Cooperative multi-CTA cluster panel (TSQR row-split, EXACT Householder layout) for n=512(K=2)/1024(K=4); single-CTA panel kept for n<=352. Thread-block cluster of K CTAs cooperatively factors one matrix's panel by splitting the m rows; cross-CTA norm/trailing/Gram reductions via DSMEM (cluster.sync+map_shared_rank). Validates CLEAN (22 tests + diff + invariance + offgrid). Fixed a pivot-row DSMEM-read vs owner-update race (B>=640 mixed factor residual 0.65/1.73 -> folded v[k]=1 pivot row into owner CTA local partial -> clean). Geomean 8023us vs parent 7468 = 7.4pct REGRESSION. nsys n512: panel_factor_cluster_kernel 682us avg (16 inst, 70.3pct) vs parent single-CTA panel 498us avg -- the per-column cluster.sync overhead + K=2 modest row-split outweighs the row-parallelism gain at n512. Trailing GEMMs unchanged.

K sweep: n=512 K=4, n=1024 K=8, + __launch_bounds__(128,8). n512 K=2->4 REGRESSED 15887->19301us (cluster-sync cost grows with K, outweighs occupancy gain on smaller panel); n1024 K=4->8 IMPROVED 12369->11868us. Net geomean 8440 vs trial1 8023 (worse). Validates CLEAN. KEY DIAGNOSIS from trial-1 ncu (K=2): cluster RAISED active-warps/sched 2.53->4.4 and compute-throughput 24pct->40pct (brief occupancy hypothesis CONFIRMED) but regs jumped 32->56 and SMEM (Block Limit 5) bounds occupancy; per-column cluster.sync latency is the dominant cost and scales with K. Best per-n so far: K=2 n512, K=8 n1024. Next: cut cluster.sync count per column and per-n K.

Per-n cluster K (K=2 n512, K=8 n1024) on the proven 3-cluster-sync structure. Geomean 7933 vs parent 7468 = 6.2pct regression (best cooperative-cluster trial). n512=15906us (K=2; K=4 regressed to 19301), n1024=11847us (K=8 best of {4,8}). EXPLORED+REVERTED: cutting per-column cluster.sync 3->2 (form-v+end-of-col to __syncthreads) FAULTS at B>=96 (cudaErrorLaunchFailure) -- cluster.sync is load-bearing for DSMEM coherence/residency, not just data-dep. MEASURED CONCLUSION: exact-Householder cooperative cluster's mandatory per-column cross-CTA sync latency exceeds the occupancy gain (ncu confirmed active-warps 2.53->4.4); trails single-CTA panel ~6pct. Next bet: TSQR-HR (independent local block QRs, zero per-column cross-CTA sync) + Householder reconstruction.

Chunked trailing-update (WCH=8): accumulate the rem trailing dot-products in chunks of 8 (wacc[8] not wacc[32]) to bound the register working set, killing the local-memory spill ncu flagged (cluster was 56 regs; parent 38pct local loads spilled). ONE cross-cluster sync still covers all rem. HUGE jump: geomean 7933->7524 (parent 7468, now only 0.7pct off, 17.44x over baseline). n512 15906->14165 (K=2), n1024 11847->11186 (K=8). Validates CLEAN. Confirms brief occupancy thesis: register pressure was the binding limit on the cooperative kernel; cutting the spill nearly closes the gap. Open: profile to confirm regs/occupancy; sweep WCH; re-test larger K for n512 now that regs are lower; tune __launch_bounds.

Re-test K=4 for n=512 with the spill gone (trial 4 fixed it): STILL regresses. n512 14165->16976 (K=2->4), geomean 7524->7992. Per-column 4-way cluster.sync cost still dominates the occupancy gain at n512. K=2 optimal for n512. ncu(trial4 K=2): SMEM Block Limit 5 is the binding occupancy limit (regs 64, spill 0, compute 49pct, active-warps 4.33, duration 766us/inst). Raising occupancy via K does NOT pay -- the wall is cluster.sync latency. Open: reduce SMEM/CTA another way (shrink gloc) to lift 5->6 blocks without raising K; threads=256; nsys to compare cluster panel 766us vs parent 498us per-instance.

K=16 for n=1024: regresses. n1024 11186->12886 (K=8->16), geomean 7524->7785. 16-way per-column cluster.sync exceeds occupancy gain. K-SWEEP COMPLETE: n512 optimal K=2 (K=4 worse), n1024 optimal K=8 (K=4 and K=16 both worse) -- a per-n sweet-spot balancing occupancy vs cluster.sync. Best config = trial 4 (K=2 n512, K=8 n1024) = 7524us, 0.7pct off parent 7468. Next: revert to best config; reduce SMEM/CTA (shrink gloc Gram buffer) to lift n512 occupancy 5->6 blocks without raising K; nsys cluster-panel vs parent 498us/inst.

HYBRID panel routing: cooperative cluster for TALL panels (m>=256, K=2 n512/K=8 n1024), single-CTA for short panels (m<256, no cluster.sync). Mixing the two kernels per-panel is correct (identical (H,tau)+V+T layout), validates CLEAN. *** WIN: geomean 7248us vs parent 7468 = 2.9pct FASTER, 18.10x over baseline 131187. *** n512 14165->13030, n1024 11186->10700. The cooperative cluster only pays off where the panel is tall enough that the row-split occupancy gain exceeds the fixed per-column cluster.sync cost; confining it to those panels makes the brief's cooperative multi-CTA panel BEAT the single-CTA-only lineage. nsys: all-cluster n512 panel 573us/inst vs parent 498us -- the gap was small-panel cluster.sync overhead the hybrid removes. Open: sweep the m>=256 threshold (per n); larger K for the tall panels only (now that short panels are off the cluster, K=4 on the first 1-2 panels may pay).

Hybrid threshold n512 mhyb=384, n1024 mhyb=512. n512 256->384 IMPROVED 13030->12630 (crossover higher than 256). n1024 384->512 slightly worse 10617->10656 (n1024 optimum ~384). Geomean 7163 = NEW BEST, 4.1pct faster than parent 7468, 18.31x over baseline 131187. Per-n hybrid crossover: n512 wants mhyb>=384, n1024 ~384. Next: push n512 higher (448/512), n1024 back to 384.

Hybrid threshold n512 mhyb=448, n1024 mhyb=384 = NEW BEST. n512 384->448 flat (12630->12624, plateau). n1024 512->384 IMPROVED 10656->10605 (384 confirmed n1024 optimum). Geomean 7158 = 4.1pct faster than parent 7468, 18.33x over baseline 131187. Cluster now runs only on the 1-3 TALLEST panels per matrix (n512: m>=448 = first 3 of 16; n1024: m>=384) where row-split occupancy clears the cluster.sync cost. Need a full validate at final config to confirm. Open: larger K (K=4) on the 1-3 tall panels only (no small-panel penalty now); n512 mhyb=512 (cluster only the single tallest panel).

K=4 on the hybrid (n512 tall panels only, mhyb=448): STILL regresses. n512 12624->12966, geomean 7158->7222. With small panels already on single-CTA, the 4-way per-column cluster.sync still dominates even on the tallest panels. K=2 robustly optimal for n512 across all hybrid thresholds. Best remains trial 10 (K=2 n512/K=8 n1024, mhyb 448/384) = 7158us = 4.1pct faster than parent, validated CLEAN. Revert to K=2.

n1024 hybrid mhyb=640: slightly worse than 384. n1024 384->640 regressed 10605->10834 (re-run; first run hit a transient GPU-contention anomaly reading 1866us geomean / shape0 123->10us, discarded as environment noise). n1024 optimum confirmed mhyb=384. Geomean 7184 vs trial-10 best 7158. Best config stays trial 10 (n512 mhyb=448/K=2, n1024 mhyb=384/K=8) = 7158us, 4.1pct faster than parent, validated CLEAN. CAUTION: a benchmark anomaly (4x-too-fast, all shapes incl n=32) occurred once -- treat sub-noise deltas skeptically; the win is robust at ~4pct (n512 12624 vs parent-lineage, n1024 10605).

FUSED next-column norm in the cluster kernel (cluster.sync 4->3 per column). Compute column k+1's norm at the END of column k's body into clred[NSLOT], published by the end-of-column cluster.sync; next column reads its cross-summed norm at the top WITHOUT a dedicated norm cross-sync (brief-2's single-CTA fusion trick adapted cross-CTA). Runs the fused norm for ALL paths (degenerate nz==false column's k+1 still needs it). Fixed a load->norm read-before-write race (missing __syncthreads after SMEM load). Validates CLEAN. WIN: geomean 7158->7128 = 4.5pct faster than parent 7468, 18.41x over baseline. n512 12624->12570, n1024 10605->10495. Directly attacks the cluster.sync wall. Open: now try cutting form-v sync #2 (next-col alpha read is now protected by the fused-norm end sync) -> 3->2 syncs; re-sweep mhyb with the cheaper cluster.

Attempted to cut the form-v cluster.sync to __syncthreads (3->2 cluster.sync/col), now that the fused-norm end-of-col sync protects the next-column alpha/clred reads. Test shapes (22) PASS but the diff_correctness guard HANGS (validate TIMEOUT rc=124) on the large benchmark shapes (n512 B640) -- a cluster-barrier DEADLOCK at scale, same failure class as trial-3's form-v cut (which faulted at B>=96). CONFIRMS: the form-v cluster.sync is load-bearing for cluster-barrier/DSMEM-coherence semantics, not just data dependency -- it cannot be reduced to __syncthreads. Reverted to trial-13 (3 cluster.sync/col, geomean 7128 = 4.5pct faster than parent, the keeper). Cluster.sync floor for this kernel structure is 3/column (form-v, trailing-cross, end-of-col-fused-norm).

Re-sweep hybrid threshold with the cheaper (3-sync, fused-norm) cluster: mhyb=256 both n. Geomean 7199 vs trial-13 best 7128. n512 mhyb=256 gives 12926 (vs 12570 at mhyb=448) WORSE; n1024 mhyb=256 gives 10566 (vs 10495 at mhyb=384) WORSE. The fused-norm lowered cluster cost uniformly but did NOT shift the crossover -- n512=448, n1024=384 remain optimal (trial 13). Confirms trial-13 (geomean 7128, 4.5pct faster than parent) is the keeper. Reverted to trial-13 thresholds.

DELIVERED a WIN: the cooperative multi-CTA-per-matrix cluster panel BEATS the global-best single-CTA-only parent. Best = HEAD 97d5392 (trial 13), geomean 7128us (re-confirmed 7134, <0.1pct noise) vs parent 7468 = 4.5pct faster, 18.41x over baseline 131187. Validated CLEAN (22 tests + diff + invariance + offgrid) at the final config. Submit-worthy.

APPROACH (the brief's 'parallelize across the cluster, exact Householder layout' route -- more tractable than TSQR-HR, and it won): thread-block cluster of K CTAs cooperatively factors ONE matrix's panel by splitting the m rows across the cluster; cross-CTA norm/trailing/Gram reductions via DSMEM (cluster.sync + map_shared_rank, sm_100a). Emits the EXACT geqrf (H,tau)+V+T (no reconstruction needed); trailing update stays the parent's FP32 cuBLAS bmm.

WHAT MOVED THE NUMBER (all measured):
1. First cut (all-cluster, K=2 n512/K=4 n1024): 8023us, a 7.4pct REGRESSION -- the per-column cluster.sync cost exceeded the occupancy gain. ncu confirmed the brief's thesis though: active-warps/sched 2.53->4.4, compute 24->40pct.
2. Chunked trailing-update (wacc[8] not wacc[32]) killed the local-mem spill ncu flagged -> 7524us (0.7pct off parent). Register/spill was the binding limit.
3. HYBRID panel routing (THE BREAKTHROUGH): cluster ONLY for tall panels (m>=mhyb), single-CTA for short panels. The cluster pays off only where the panel is tall enough that the row-split occupancy gain clears the fixed per-column cluster.sync cost; confining it there -> 7248us, FIRST BEAT of the parent. nsys proves it: on n512 the 3 tallest panels run on the cluster (730us/inst, vs ~900us each on single-CTA) and the 13 short panels on single-CTA.
4. Per-n hybrid threshold sweep: n512 mhyb=448, n1024 mhyb=384 optimal -> 7158us.
5. FUSED next-column norm (cluster.sync 4->3/col): compute col k+1's norm at end of col k, published by the end-of-col sync -> 7128us (final).

DEAD ENDS (measured): K>2 for n512 always regresses (4-way cluster.sync too costly, even on tall panels only); K=16 for n1024 regresses (K=8 optimal). Cutting cluster.sync below 3/col (form-v -> __syncthreads) HANGS/faults at B>=96 -- the cluster.sync is load-bearing for cluster-barrier/DSMEM coherence, not just data-dep; 3/col is the floor for this structure.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not closed -- worth fresh briefs):
- SMEM is STILL the binding occupancy limit (Block Limit Shared Mem=5, achieved occupancy 27pct, active-warps 4.33). Shave the cluster kernel's 38KB/CTA below 38KB (the 4KB gloc Gram buffer -> move partial Grams to a small global scratch; or drop the CLDC pad) to reach 6+ blocks/SM -- direct occupancy headroom.
- TSQR-HR reconstruction (the brief's OTHER route, NOT built): independent local block QRs with zero per-column cross-CTA sync + Ballard/Demmel no-pivot-LU-of-(Q-S) reconstruction. My analysis suggests ~2x panel work (local QR + form-Q + LU) for an occupancy-only gain, so uncertain ROI, but it removes the per-column cluster.sync wall entirely -- a genuinely different structure worth a measurement.
- threads/CTA sweep (128 fixed) on the cluster kernel now that only tall panels use it (256 threads = 1 row/thread on the m=512 panel).
- n1024 currently K=8/mhyb=384; its panel split could be re-tuned independently.
- The trailing FP32 cuBLAS GEMM is ~33pct of n512 time and untouched (on-brief = panel); other briefs own trailing precision.
